uncited: This method computes the ensemble-averaged transmittance of participating media by modeling the line-averaged micro-scale density as a Gamma-distributed random variable.
No persistent data structures are required.
The method computes parameters on the fly.
A special case where the spectral exponent $\beta = 1$ (pink noise).
Requires basic arithmetic operations and a logarithm/exponential.
Provides a closed-form solution for non-exponential transmittance.
Requires tuning of three parameters ($\mu_\sigma, C, \beta$).
It is part of the broader effort to model light transport in participating media with fractal $1/f^\beta$ noise density distributions.

The Gamma-distributed model was proposed by Davis and Mineev-Weinstein [2011] to address the limitations of the Gaussian approximation in the path integral framework for non-exponential media [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that Davis and Mineev-Weinstein [2011] proposed the Gamma-distributed model to counteract artifacts (specifically negative extinction values) arising from the Gaussian approximation, which is limited because it allows non-physical negative values. The evidence confirms the model is used for non-exponential media (fractal 1/f beta noise) and provides the specific mathematical forms for the transmittance and shape parameter mentioned in the claim.
